definition: A macromolecule made by joining a very large number of small molecules, called monomers, with covalent bonds.
A reaction in which two reactant molecules combine to form a single product; in an alkene, the $\ce{C=C}$ double bond becomes a single bond.
A polymer formed when monomers with a $\ce{C=C}$ double bond join, each double bond becoming a single bond; it is the only product, so the atom economy is 100%.
A reaction in which two molecules join together and a small molecule, such as water, is released.
A polymer, such as a polyester or polyamide, formed from monomers with two functional groups each, with a small molecule such as water released at every link.
The breaking of a bond in a compound by reaction with water; it is the reverse of a condensation reaction.
